scenes.heading: How Photosynthesis Works
scenes.text: The recipe plants use to turn sunlight into food.
scenes.narration: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to turn sunlight into food. Let's see how it works.

scenes.heading: What plants need
scenes.narration: Every plant needs three ingredients: sunlight, water from the soil, and carbon dioxide from the air.

scenes.heading: Catching the light
scenes.text: Chlorophyll, the green pigment, absorbs sunlight.
scenes.narration: Leaves contain chlorophyll, a green pigment that captures light energy from the sun.

scenes.heading: Light powers the reaction
scenes.text: Sunlight splits water into hydrogen and oxygen.
scenes.narration: Light energy splits water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen. The oxygen is released.

scenes.heading: Building sugar
scenes.text: Carbon dioxide becomes glucose, the plant's food.
scenes.narration: Carbon dioxide is combined with hydrogen to build glucose, a sugar the plant uses for energy and growth.

scenes.heading: Oxygen for us
scenes.text: Every breath you take came from a leaf.
scenes.narration: The oxygen released by photosynthesis fills the atmosphere. Nearly every breath you take comes from it.

scenes.heading: Feeding the world
scenes.text: Farms and forests run on captured sunlight.
scenes.narration: Crops, forests, and ocean plankton all photosynthesize, forming the base of nearly every food chain.

scenes.heading: The big picture
scenes.text: Sunlight in, food and oxygen out.
scenes.narration: In short: sunlight in, food and oxygen out. Photosynthesis powers life on Earth.
